article_content: NEW YORK (CNN) -- The death of a 12-year-old student in Brooklyn from a MRSA staph infection has triggered concerns among parents and students throughout the New York City school system, prompting an official response. Omar Rivera, a 12-year-old seventh-grader in New York, died on October 14 from the drug-resistant staph infection. Rivera, a student at Intermediate School 211, succumbed to the infection on October 14, according to the New York City school superintendent, although investigators could not determine where he contracted it. MRSA, or methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, is responsible for a significant number of deaths in the United States annually, according to some data. 'It is often impossible to pinpoint how someone contracts the infection,' stated New York City Health Commissioner Tom Frieden. 'An infection like this in a child is extremely rare. Fatal infections in children occur at a rate of approximately 1 in a million. It is a terrible tragedy, and we extend our deepest sympathies to the family.' The Office of School Health sent letters to parents on Thursday, informing them of Rivera's death. Despite assurances from health officials that Rivera's death was an isolated incident, several parents chose to keep their children home from IS 211, which remained open on Friday following the announcement of Rivera's death. The Health Department stated, 'We have no reason to believe that other children or school employees face an increased risk of staph infection.' However, department officials advised at a press conference on Friday that people should reduce skin-to-skin contact, wash hands regularly, and avoid sharing items like towels and razors. Nearly 90% of resistant staph infections are related to hospitals or health-care settings, according to Frieden. 'Hospitals must take this seriously and continue to improve their prevention and treatment methods for staph infections,' he said. The CDC reports that 25 to 30 percent of the population carries the staph bacteria -- a common cause of infection. While these infections are usually minor, invasive MRSA infections, caused by drug-resistant staph, can become fatal. Dr. Julie Gerberding, the director of the CDC, notes that these infections are not new. 'It's important to remember that many of these infections are the same ones mothers have dealt with for decades. They're very preventable,' she says. 'If you notice a skin infection where the redness is expanding or accompanied by significant swelling around the wound, or if the person has a fever, seek medical attention immediately. However, most of the time, these issues can be managed with the same common-sense approach we've used for years.' Pat Mshar, an epidemiologist for Connecticut's Department of Health, emphasized that hospitals account for the highest rate of MRSA deaths -- 58 percent. 'A healthy person in the community, such as a high school student, can generally be treated effectively without adverse outcomes,' she said. As long as an infected student seeks treatment, covers any open cuts or lesions, and avoids direct skin contact with other students, 'it's OK to attend school.' She noted that recent reports of MRSA cases and student deaths have increased public concern. 'Parents are more aware of MRSA now than ever before,' she said. For more information, consult MayoClinic.com's Q&A on MRSA, the Centers for Disease Control's Invasive MRSA Fact Sheet, their advice on MRSA in schools, and the Journal of the American Medical Association's Patient Page on MRSA.

Omar Rivera, oo ah arday 12 jir ah oo fasalka toddobaad ka dhigta New York, ayaa dhintay Oktoobar 14-keedii, cudurka staph ee daawada u adkaysta. Rivera, oo arday ka ahaa Dugsiga Dhexe ee 211, ayaa u geeriyooday caabuqa Oktoobar 14-keedii, sida uu sheegay kormeeraha iskuullada Magaalada New York, in kastoo baadhayaashu ay awoodi waayeen inay xaqiijiyaan halka uu cudurku ku dhacay. MRSA, ama methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, ayaa sabab u ah tiro badan oo dhimasho ah oo ka dhacda Maraykanka sannadkii, sida ay sheegayaan xogaha qaar. 'Badanaa suurtagal maaha in la ogaado sida qofku u qaado caabuqa,' ayuu yiri Guddoomiyaha Caafimaadka ee Magaalada New York Tom Frieden. In kasta oo ay jireen damaanado ka imanaya saraakiisha caafimaadka oo ah in dhimashada Rivera ay ahayd dhacdo gooni ah, haddana waalidiin dhowr ah ayaa go'aansaday inay carruurtooda ka joojiyaan Dugsiga Dhexe ee 211, kaas oo furanaa Jimcihii ka dib markii lagu dhawaaqay geerida Rivera. Waaxda Caafimaadka ayaa sheegtay, 'Ma lihin sabab aan ku rumaysanno in carruur kale ama shaqaalaha iskuulku ay wajahayaan khatar sare oo ah caabuqa staph.' Si kastaba ha ahaatee, saraakiisha waaxda ayaa ku taliyay shir jaraa'id oo ay qabteen Jimcihii in dadku ay yareeyaan is-taabashada maqaarka, si joogto ah u dhaqaan gacmahooda, ayna ka fogaadaan inay wadaagaan alaabada sida tuwaalada iyo mindiyaha xiirta. Ku dhowaad 90% caabuqyada staph ee u adkaysta daawooyinka ayaa la xidhiidha isbitaallada ama goobaha daryeelka caafimaadka, sida uu sheegay Frieden. 'Isbitaalladu waa inay arrintan si dhab ah u qaataan oo ay sii wadaan inay horumariyaan hababkooda looga hortago iyo daweynta caabuqyada staph,' ayuu yidhi. CDC waxay ku warramaysaa in 25 ilaa 30 boqolkiiba dadweynaha ay qabaan bakteeriyada staph, taasoo ah sabab caadi ah oo caabuq. In kasta oo caabuqyadani badanaa ay yihiin kuwo fudud, caabuqyada MRSA ee faafa, ee ay sababto staph-ka daawada u adkaysta, waxay noqon karaan kuwo dilaa ah. Dr. Julie Gerberding, oo ah agaasimaha CDC, ayaa xustay in caabuqyadani aysan ahayn kuwo cusub. 'Waxaa muhiim ah in la xasuusto in caabuqyo badan oo ka mid ah kuwan ay yihiin kuwii ay hooyooyinku la tacaalayeen tobannaan sano. Aad bay u fududahay in laga hortago,' ayay tidhi. 'Haddii aad aragto caabuq maqaarka ah oo casaan uu sii fidaya ama ay weheliso barar weyn oo ku wareegsan boogta, ama haddii qofku qabo qandho, isla markiiba raadso daryeel caafimaad. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, inta badan, arrimahan waxaa lagu maareyn karaa habka caadiga ah ee aan isticmaalnay sanado badan.' Pat Mshar, oo ah khabiir ku takhasusay cudurrada faafa oo ka tirsan Waaxda Caafimaadka ee Connecticut, ayaa ku nuuxnuuxsatay in isbitaalladu ay yihiin meesha ugu badan ee laga helo dhimashada MRSA, taasoo ah 58 boqolkiiba. 'Qofka caafimaadka qaba ee ku nool bulshada, sida ardayga dugsiga sare, guud ahaan si wax ku ool ah ayaa loo daweyn karaa iyada oo aan wax dhibaato ah dhicin,' ayay tidhi. Ilaa inta ardayga uu qabo caabuqa uu raadsado daweyn, uu daboolo jeexjeexyada furan, kana fogaado taabashada tooska ah ee maqaarka ardayda kale, 'way fiican tahay in iskuulka la aado.' Waxay xustay in warbixinnadii ugu dambeeyay ee tirada MRSA iyo dhimashada ardayda ay kordhisay welwelka dadweynaha. 'Waalidiintu way ka warqabaan MRSA hadda in ka badan sidii hore abid,' ayay tidhi. Wixii macluumaad dheeraad ah, ka eeg MayoClinic.com Q&A-da ku saabsan MRSA, Xaqiiqda ku saabsan MRSA ee Faafa ee Xarumaha Xakamaynta iyo Kahortagga Cudurrada, taladooda ku saabsan MRSA ee iskuullada, iyo Bogga Bukaanka ee MRSA ee Joornaalka Ururka Caafimaadka ee Maraykanka.

article_content: Northampton narrowly defeated London Irish at the Madejski Stadium, with Luther Burrell's try proving decisive as they reclaimed the Aviva Premiership lead. Following Bath's dominant win against Saracens earlier in the day, Northampton struggled but ultimately secured their fourth victory of the season. Burrell, the England centre, scored the game's only try in the 36th minute in what was otherwise a lackluster contest. Northampton's return to the top of the Aviva Premiership was secured by Burrell's try. Although Burrell displayed power in scoring, the game was marred by handling errors that could impact his chances for selection in the upcoming QBE Internationals. Fly-half Stephen Myler accumulated 14 points, consisting of four penalties and a conversion. Northampton held a 10-0 lead at halftime, but London Irish rallied, with Shane Geraghty's four penalties earning them a bonus point. Samu Manoa demonstrated his strength with an early powerful run through London Irish's defense. However, a poor pass from Burrell squandered a potential overlap for Northampton, who were without the injured England forwards Tom Wood and Dylan Hartley. Northampton intensified pressure at the scrum, leading to Myler's first penalty. Shane Geraghty's four penalties ultimately secured London Irish a valuable bonus point. The game's untidy nature persisted with Geraghty missing an easy kick, and Courtney Lawes subsequently tackled the former England fly-half. Ken Pisi's significant hit enabled Northampton to transition from defense to attack, but London Irish quickly recovered, maintaining the stalemate. Northampton again pressured the London Irish 22, but handling errors, particularly from Burrell, hindered their progress. However, Burrell redeemed himself by scoring a try after a swift counter-attack, initiated by a loose kick from London Irish, caught them off guard. James Craig of Northampton outjumped his London Irish opponent at the lineout. Myler, Ken Pisi, and George North contributed to the attack before Burrell opted to charge forward, overcoming Geraghty and a last-ditch tackle from Tomas O'Leary. The third quarter largely involved a kicking exchange between Geraghty and Myler in a match that continued to disappoint. A collision between North and Andrew Fenby resulted in Fenby securing a remarkable catch. The third quarter was defined by the kicking duel between Geraghty and Myler. With Geraghty's fourth penalty, the likelihood of another try seemed minimal. London Irish continued to challenge Northampton, though Geraghty's missed drop-goal and long-range penalty hampered their efforts. Late in the game, Burrell nearly scored again, but a poor pass ruined a chance for Ben Foden. Fittingly, Myler concluded the match with a final penalty.

article_content: Headteachers are reporting a growing trend: more students are foregoing UK institutions like Oxford and Cambridge to pursue their education overseas, seeking better value for their money. The steep £9,000 annual tuition fees at UK universities are a significant deterrent. Independent schools note an increasing number of their students are accepting offers from universities abroad, especially in the United States. A key advantage cited by many is that overseas universities frequently provide students with more direct interaction with their professors compared to the majority of UK universities. This shift occurs as the UCAS deadline for British university applications nears. Keith Budge, headteacher at Bedales School in Hampshire, observed a 'discernible increase' in students opting for international study, rising from approximately five percent to nine percent in recent years. Richard Harman, head of Uppingham School in Rutland, mentioned a student choosing Stanford University in California over Cambridge. Data from November revealed an unprecedented number of British students heading to American universities, motivated by concerns about escalating costs and the perceived quality of UK degree programs. Over 10,000 British students enrolled in US institutions, which often offer substantial scholarship opportunities, during the 2013-14 academic year. The Institute for International Education (IIE) reported this as an eight percent increase from the previous year, marking the largest annual rise in a decade. Stanford University is one example of an attractive alternative. The top five US universities for UK students in 2013-14 were Harvard, Columbia, New York University, University of California Berkeley, and Yale. Last year's analysis of data from the Government website Unistats revealed significant disparities in contact hours; some students receive less than half the lecture, seminar, and tutorial time compared to peers studying the same subject at other UK universities. Back in 2012, Anthony Seldon, Master of Wellington College in Berkshire, cautioned that UK institutions' 'malaise' was pushing students to seek opportunities across the Atlantic. He criticized British universities for insufficient lecturer contact and a 'perfunctory interest' in sports and the arts.

article_content: By Mario Ledwith. Justin Welby, the Archbishop of Canterbury, has warned against the 'ridiculous' materialistic excesses of Christmas. According to the Archbishop of Canterbury, increased financial pressure leading up to Christmas ‘spoils life’ for families across the UK. Justin Welby criticized the festive period as ‘over the top’ and said that high spending in an attempt to create the perfect Christmas risks making life miserable. In a frank admission, the former oil executive said nobody would ‘pay attention’ to his message about the obsession with material goods. Archbishop Welby warned hard-pressed families across the UK: ‘Save up for the Christmas budget, be sensible, don’t put pressure on your finances – don’t make your life miserable with Christmas.’ His description of the festive period as ‘absurd and ridiculous’ follows research suggesting the average family spends £1,000 on Christmas. The stark assessment of Christmas celebrations is his first comment on the Christian festival since becoming Archbishop. He said: ‘The Christian aspect of Christmas isn’t what’s getting people into debt. ‘It’s the whole mercantile trading, shopping, over-the-top nature of it, so I don’t feel guilty about it.’ Admitting that the obsession with shopping is unlikely to wane, he said that people should show ‘love and affection rather than trying to buy love and affection’. He added: ‘You can’t buy it, you can show it, and when you show it, it comes back to you with interest. Share love and affection with reasonable gifts that demonstrate you really care for someone’. During the interview for ITV’s The Martin Lewis Money Show, the Archbishop admitted his comments were unlikely to make a difference. He said: ‘It’s a cliché of modern life that someone gets up and says Christmas is becoming very materialistic, as though it wasn’t 300 years ago. 'Yes, obviously the secular over-the-topness, everything you have to have, new clothes you have to have, new this, new that, new the other, is ridiculous, it’s absurd, it shouldn’t happen. ‘It’s obviously not what Christmas is about but to be absolutely honest there’s not much point in saying it because nobody’s going to pay attention.’ 'It's obviously not what Christmas is about': Thousands of shoppers trudge along Oxford Street in the gathering gloom last December. Welby called for people to show 'love and affection' rather than trying to buy it.

Wuxuu yiri: 'Qaybta Masiixiga ee Kirismaska maaha waxa dadka gelinaya deyn. ‘Waa ganacsi dhan, wax iibsasho, dabeecad xad dhaaf ah, markaa anigu kama xumaayo.’ Isagoo qiray in ku dheggganaanta wax iibsiga ay u badan tahay inay yaraato, wuxuu sheegay in dadku ay muujiyaan 'jacayl iyo kalgacal halkii ay ka iibsan lahaayeen jacayl iyo kalgacal'. Wuxuu ku daray: ‘Ma iibsan kartid, waad muujin kartaa, markaad muujisidna, waxay kuugu soo laabanaysaa iyadoo dulsaar leh. La wadaag jacayl iyo kalgacal hadiyado macquul ah oo muujinaya inaad runtii qof u danaynayso’. Intii lagu guda jiray wareysiga barnaamijka ITV ee The Martin Lewis Money Show, Archbishop-ka wuxuu qiray in hadalladiisu aysan u badan tahay inay wax isbeddel ah sameeyaan. Wuxuu yiri: 'Waa hadal caadi ah oo nolosha casriga ah ah in qof kaco oo yiraahdo Kirismasku wuxuu noqonayaa mid aad u hanti badan, sidii oo aanu ahayn 300 oo sano ka hor. 'Haa, sida iska cad, xad-gudubka cilmaaniga ah, wax kasta oo ay tahay inaad haysato, dhar cusub oo ay tahay inaad haysato, kan cusub, ka cusub, kan kale ee cusub, waa wax laga xumaado, waa wax aan macno lahayn, ma dhici karto. ‘Sida iska cad maaha waxa Kirismasku ku saabsan yahay laakiin si daacad ah haddii aan u hadlo wax badan oo micno ah ma jiraan in la sheego maxaa yeelay qofna dheg jalaq uma siin doono.’ 'Sida iska cad maaha waxa Kirismasku ku saabsan yahay': Kumanaan qof oo wax iibsanaya ayaa ku lugeynaya wadada Oxford iyadoo mugdigu soo ururayo bishii Disembar ee la soo dhaafay. Welby wuxuu ugu baaqay dadka inay muujiyaan 'jacayl iyo kalgacal' halkii ay isku dayi lahaayeen inay iibsadaan.

article_content: Senator Mary Landrieu's reelection campaign is undergoing a leadership shift with Election Day less than a month away. According to reports initially from the New Orleans Times-Picayune on Wednesday, the Louisiana Democrat has revamped her campaign staff. She's appointed a new campaign manager and enlisted the assistance of both former and current Senate personnel to help her navigate challenges from two Republican contenders in Louisiana's open primary. These adjustments occur as Landrieu's chances of securing 50% of the vote—necessary to circumvent a runoff election—appear to be diminishing. Ryan Berni, who managed her brother, New Orleans Mayor Mitch Landrieu's successful reelection effort earlier this year, is now spearheading the campaign. Landrieu has also reached out to Norma Jane Sabiston, her previous chief of staff, for strategic guidance. Adam Sullivan, the current campaign manager, will transition into the role of senior advisor to the campaign. Fabien Levy, Landrieu's campaign spokesperson, declined to specify the precise reason for Sullivan's replacement, stating in an email to CNN that Senator Landrieu consistently calls upon trusted, long-term advisors to assist in the final month of her races, aiming for victory on November 4. Furthermore, two of Landrieu's Senate staffers, her state director and Washington communications director, are temporarily stepping away from their Senate duties to dedicate their efforts to her campaign. Landrieu is experiencing a difficult reelection campaign, and her new team will be tasked with helping her surpass the crucial 50% mark required to avoid a runoff in December. According to a recent CNN/ORC poll, this goal seems challenging, as Landrieu's support stands at 43%, closely followed by Representative Bill Cassidy at 40%. A runoff election between Landrieu and Cassidy could potentially benefit Cassidy, who could consolidate votes previously allocated to the third candidate, Tea Party Republican Rob Maness. However, the election is projected to be tight. The CNN/ORC poll suggests that Cassidy would only hold a narrow 3-point advantage over the incumbent Senator in a runoff scenario.

Waxay magacaabatay maareeye cusub oo ololaha, waxayna codsatay caawimaad ka timid shaqaalihii hore iyo kuwa hadda ee Aqalka Senate-ka si ay uga caawiyaan inay ka gudubto caqabadaha uga imanaya laba musharax oo Jamhuuri ah doorashada furan ee Louisiana. Intaa waxaa dheer, laba ka mid ah shaqaalaha Senate-ka ee Landrieu, agaasimaheeda gobolka iyo agaasimaha isgaarsiinta ee Washington, ayaa si ku meel gaar ah uga tagaya waajibaadkooda Senate-ka si ay ugu huraan dadaalkooda ololaheeda. Sida lagu sheegay ra'yi ururin dhowaan ay samaysay CNN/ORC, hadafkani wuxuu u muuqdaa mid adag, maadaama taageerada Landrieu ay taagan tahay 43%, waxaana si dhow ula socda Wakiil Bill Cassidy oo haysta 40%. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, doorashadu waxaa la filayaa inay noqoto mid adag. Ra'yi ururinta CNN/ORC waxay soo jeedinaysaa in Cassidy uu kaliya ku hayn doono faa'iido yar oo 3-dhibcood ah oo ka sarreysa Senatarka xilka haya marka la gaaro xaalad wareeg ah.

article_content: Queen Maxima of the Netherlands, a member of the House of Orange-Nassau, seemed to embody her married name during a recent visit. The Dutch royal, born in Argentina, looked patriotic in an orange top as she visited the Veenkoloniaal Museum in Veendam with her husband, King Willem-Alexander. Maxima, who became Queen Consort of the Netherlands in 2013, paired her tangerine and grey Natan dress with matching orange suede heels and her signature chunky jewelry. She looked glamorous in her tangerine and grey Natan dress during her visit to Veendam. The royal couple stopped to greet well-wishers upon arriving at the museum. Maxima received a bouquet of tulips, a fittingly patriotic flower. Accompanied by Veendam's mayor, Sipke Swierstra, they toured the exhibits, which collectively narrated the history of the nearby Groningen peat district. The Groningen peat moors played a vital role in the area's early industrial development. These moors, over 5,000 years old, facilitated trade between the Netherlands, its neighbors, and the UK. Crucially for the museum, the peat also preserved numerous artifacts, including the remarkably well-preserved remains of a wagon wheel dating back to 2,500 BC. Maxima appeared to thoroughly enjoy her tour, observing several paintings of the peat villages that once dotted the landscape and engaging the curators with insightful questions. She paired her dress with a charcoal hat and orange earrings for the occasion. Maxima also met farmers and volunteers from the Groningen area after her museum tour. She received a floral tribute of patriotic tulips from well-wishers. The Dutch royals also visited a nearby cultural center, where they met local farmers and museum volunteers who were assisting with unpacking boxes of maps. However, all eyes were drawn to Maxima, who radiated energy as she walked through the crowds in her striking color-block dress, which she has worn before. The Natan dress, a Belgian label that originated in a small Brussels atelier in 1930, is a staple in her wardrobe. After struggling for nearly half a century, Edouard Vermeulen took over the brand and transformed it into a prominent fashion house. The label, which designed the dress worn by Belgium's Queen Mathilde for her 2001 wedding, also created the gown Maxima wore for her engagement portrait in 2002. Eleven years later, the Queen Consort of the Netherlands wore a nude silk gown by the same label for her first public appearance on the balcony after her inauguration. Maxima, escorted by Mayor Sipke Swierstra, seemed amused by something in the crowd. Her ensemble was carefully coordinated, featuring bright orange and grey elements. King Willem-Alexander paused to shake hands with a young girl with a disability. Maxima showcased her statement jewelry and a wide-brimmed charcoal grey felt hat.

Boqoradda u dhalatay Netherlands, ee ku dhalatay Argentina, waxay u ekayd mid waddaniyad jecel iyada oo ku labisan dhar oranji ah markii ay booqatay Matxafka Veenkoloniaal ee Veendam iyada iyo seygeeda, Boqor Willem-Alexander. article_content: A couple believe they may own Britain's naughtiest dog after their puppy ate through wallpaper, bricks, and even the family's new kitchen floor. Ralph, a seven-month-old spaniel, has chewed through cables and destroyed solar panels at his home in Guisborough, North Yorkshire. Despite his adorable puppy-dog eyes, owners Dean and Diane Yates say the animal regularly creates havoc in their home. Home wrecker: Ralph (left and right), the seven-month-old spaniel, has created havoc in his new home in Guisborough, North Yorkshire. Dean Yates (pictured) said his family could not resist Ralph's cute and cuddly looks and lively character when they first chose a family pet. At just weeks old, Ralph ate the wallpaper in his room under the staircase, so much so that the area is now bare. He even managed to escape upstairs and knock out their eight-year-old daughter's tooth while jumping around on her bed while she was asleep. The family quickly learned not to let Ralph in their front room after he tore up their carpet and even ate the solar panels when they tried to keep him in the garden. They also returned home one evening to find a large section of the kitchen floor pulled up, with Ralph staring mischievously at them. In the dog house: The family returned home one evening to find a large section of the kitchen floor pulled up, with Ralph staring mischievously at them. Bad dog: Ralph is pictured left with owner Diane Yates and her daughter Abigail, eight, and right with Dean Yates. Dean, 28, said: 'People warned us that spaniels were energetic dogs, but I didn't expect Ralph to be this naughty. I don't know any other dog that is like him.' 'We've never had a family dog before, so this has certainly been an experience. Our daughter Abigail picked him because she thought he looked the most fun as he was running over his brothers and sisters - we should have seen the warnings.' 'The worst incident for us has to be when we accidentally left his gate open, and when we went upstairs, he was bouncing on Abigail's bed while she was asleep and had knocked out one of her front teeth.' 'It's so hard to be annoyed at him because he is so cute, but at first, we were really scared because Abigail had blood on her face.' 'I was also pretty annoyed when he chewed through all the wires to the filter of my brand new aquarium. It cost a bomb, and he just tore straight through it.' 'We came home one day and found the kitchen floor completely torn up. He was just standing looking at us like a silent menace. I couldn't work out how he had done it as it was twice his size.' As well as the kitchen floor, Mr. Yates, a marine engineer, and his 28-year-old sales assistant wife have caught Ralph eating through bags of their toilet roll when they found it scattered around the house and garden. The pair have also caught him stealing their prepared meals from the kitchen bench. The family have had the chocolate brown sprocker - a cross between a cocker and springer spaniel - since he was ten weeks old and say that he shows no sign of calming down with age. Bad manners: Ralph was caught eating through bags of toilet roll when the family found it scattered around the house and garden. The family says Ralph managed to escape upstairs and knock their eight-year-old daughter's tooth out while jumping around on her bed while she was asleep. Abigail is pictured outdoors with her pet. Mr. Yates said: 'He would be the perfect puppy if he could just stop eating everything in sight.' 'We have a baby due in April, so the next room we were going to decorate was supposed to be the nursery - but now it's going to have to be the kitchen because he has wrecked it.' 'He's full of beans despite being walked once in the morning and twice at night. We're definitely planning on taking him to puppy classes. I really thought I'd be able to train him myself.' 'He's so lovely though; he wouldn't hurt a fly and loves affection.'

article_content: Forecasters cautioned that traveling through the southern Rocky Mountains and into the central Plains will be extremely hazardous, potentially impossible, on Tuesday due to a significant winter storm impacting large portions of the West and Midwest. The National Weather Service issued blizzard warnings stretching from southeastern Colorado across western Kansas, the Oklahoma panhandle, and into the northern reaches of Texas. They warned of expected blizzard conditions with sub-zero wind chill temperatures. Although the warnings for northeastern New Mexico had expired by late Tuesday morning, winter storm warnings remained in effect across New Mexico, Colorado, and Kansas. Reports on Tuesday indicated heavy snowfall in eastern Colorado and western Kansas, accompanied by freezing rain and sleet in south-central Kansas. Blustery winds ranging from 20 to 50 mph were also observed. The National Weather Service indicated that the most intense snowfall had likely ended as the storm moved eastward toward Oklahoma. Snowfall was expected to cease in the Rockies by late Tuesday morning but would persist across the central Plains until late in the day. Areas such as Pie Town, New Mexico, and La Junta and Springfield, Colorado, had already accumulated over 15 inches of snow since Sunday evening. Roads and highways, including interstates, were closed Monday night as at least five states grappled with heavy snow, strong winds, and icy conditions. Ariel Cohen, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service's Storm Prediction Center, reported visibility of less than a quarter-mile in parts of western Kansas and southeastern Colorado. New Mexico State Police closed Interstate 40, a major east-west route from Albuquerque to the Texas border, due to zero visibility caused by blowing snow. Interstate 25 was also shut down from north of Albuquerque to the Colorado border because of blizzard conditions and icy, snow-packed roads. The state police also closed U.S. and state highways in the northeastern part of the state. Texas authorities initially closed I-40 westbound in the Texas panhandle at New Mexico's request on Tuesday morning but reopened it by the afternoon. Gabriel Medrano, a spokesman for the state's Department of Public Safety, stated that ice was a major concern around Amarillo. They received numerous calls for stranded motorists, and troopers and the National Guard were assisting in rescuing people from their vehicles. Vehicle accidents were reported in the Amarillo area along I-40. Medrano noted receiving dozens of calls for help, mostly from individuals west of Oldham County. His agency and the Texas Department of Transportation reported that motel rooms in Tucumcari, New Mexico, the first major town on I-40 across the state line, were fully occupied because drivers were unable to proceed further on the highway. Meteorologists described the storm system as strong, creating highly dangerous conditions. While winter storms are typical, the extensive area of strong winds combined with snowfall is considered atypical. Then-Governor Rick Perry activated the Texas Military Forces as a precaution to assist on roadways, projecting snow accumulations of up to 6 inches with higher amounts in the northwest Texas Panhandle. Rick Husband Amarillo International Airport experienced flight cancellations on Tuesday morning, according to spokesman Patrick Rhodes; however, normal operations have since resumed. In the Oklahoma panhandle, U.S. highways were closed, and transportation personnel were applying salt to the roads, according to Michaelann Ootean of the Oklahoma Department of Emergency Management. The Kansas Department of Transportation reported that roads and highways were predominantly snow-packed or icy in western Kansas on Monday, including Interstate 70 and Interstate 135 through Salina. U.S. highways 50 and 54 were closed in southwest Kansas. U.S. 50 was closed due to blizzard conditions and multiple accidents in Colorado. The Colorado Department of Transportation closed highways across southeastern Colorado due to snow and icy conditions. Interstate 25 was shut southbound from Pueblo to the New Mexico border, and lodging was unavailable south of Colorado City. Northbound I-25 remained open.

article_content: This summer, beachgoers will encounter new sunscreen labels on store shelves, designed to enhance product effectiveness and ease of use. However, a consumer watchdog group reports that many sunscreens still feature SPF ratings deemed misleading and potentially hazardous by some experts. The Environmental Working Group surveyed 1,400 sunscreen products and found that most comply with federal requirements implemented last December. Warning: A consumer watchdog group stated that numerous sunscreens continue to display SPF ratings that some experts consider misleading and potentially dangerous. FDA rules prohibit terms like 'waterproof,' which regulators consider deceptive, and mandate that sunscreens protect against both ultraviolet A and B rays. Previously, certain products only blocked UVB rays, the primary cause of sunburn, while offering limited protection against UVA rays, which pose the greatest risk of skin cancer and wrinkles. Despite this improved protection, the watchdog group found that one in seven products claimed SPF ratings above 50, a level long viewed skeptically by experts. This skepticism arises partly because SPF numbers like 100 or 150 can create a false sense of security, causing users to remain in the sun longer than the lotion's protective effect lasts. Many consumers believe SPF 100 is twice as effective as SPF 50, but dermatologists assert the difference is negligible. While an SPF 50 product might block 97% of sunburn-causing rays, an SPF 100 product might block 98.5% of those rays. 'High SPF numbers are merely a gimmick,' says Marianne Berwick, professor of epidemiology at the University of New Mexico. 'Most people don't need more than SPF 30 and should reapply it every two hours.' Berwick advises using sunscreen alongside hats, clothing, and shade, which offer superior protection against ultraviolet radiation. Some dermatologists suggest there's a rationale for using higher SPF sunscreens, as users often don't apply enough lotion to achieve its full effect. 'The challenge is that beyond 50 the increase in UV protection is relatively small,' says Dr. Henry Lim, chair of dermatology at the Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit. The SPF number indicates the amount of sun exposure required to cause sunburn on sunscreen-protected skin compared to unprotected skin. For example, an SPF rating of 30 means it would take 30 times longer for a person to burn with sunscreen than without. A common misconception is that the SPF figure correlates to a specific duration in the sun. However, this is incorrect, as the level of exposure varies depending on geography, time of day, and skin complexion. In 2011, the FDA stated that 'labeling a product with a specific SPF value higher than 50 would be misleading to the consumer.' The agency proposed capping all SPF values at 50 because 'there is not sufficient data to show that products with SPF values higher than 50 provide greater protection for users.' However, regulators have faced resistance from companies like Johnson & Johnson, who argue that higher SPF products provide measurable benefits. Consequently, the FDA is still reviewing studies and comments submitted by outside parties, and there is no set deadline for finalizing an SPF cap. It took the agency decades to implement last year's sunscreen changes. The FDA initially announced its intention to draft sunscreen rules in 1978 and published them in 1999. The agency then delayed finalizing the regulations for years to address concerns from both industry and consumers. The FDA is also evaluating the safety and effectiveness of spray-on products, which use different formulations than other sun-protection solutions. Among other concerns, the agency is examining whether the sprays can be harmful when inhaled. The Environmental Working Group's survey revealed that one in four sunscreens sold in the U.S. is a spray product. 'People like the sprays because they are quick to apply and cover a large area,' said Dr. Darrell Rigel, a dermatologist in New York. 'The downside is that you usually have to apply two coats.' More than 76,000 men and women in the U.S. will be diagnosed with melanoma this year, and 9,480 are expected to die from this aggressive form of skin cancer, according to the National Cancer Institute. The disease, often linked to ultraviolet exposure, is usually curable when detected early.

Sannadkii 2011, FDA waxay sheegtay in 'ku calaamadeynta badeecada qiime gaar ah oo SPF ah oo ka sarreeya 50 ay marin habaabin doonto macaamiisha.' Si kastaba ha ahaatee, xeer ilaaliyayaashu waxay wajahdeen iska caabin ka timid shirkado sida Johnson & Johnson, kuwaas oo ku dooda in badeecooyinka SPF ee sarreeya ay bixiyaan faa'iidooyin la qiyaasi karo. Natiijo ahaan, FDA waxay weli dib u eegaysaa daraasadaha iyo faallooyinka ay soo gudbiyeen dhinacyo dibadda ah, mana jirto waqti go'an oo loogu talagalay hay'addu inay dhammaystirto xadka SPF. Waxay ku qaadatay hay'adda tobanaan sano si ay u hirgeliso isbeddellada muraayadaha qorraxda ee sannadkii hore. FDA waxay markii hore ku dhawaaqday ujeedkeeda inay qorto xeerarka muraayadaha qorraxda sannadkii 1978 waxayna daabacday sannadkii 1999. Kadib hay'addu waxay dib u dhigtay dhammaystirka xeerarka sanado badan si ay wax uga qabato welwelka ka imaanaya warshadaha iyo macaamiisha labadaba. FDA waxay sidoo kale qiimeyn ku sameyneysaa badqabka iyo waxtarka badeecooyinka lagu buufiyo, kuwaas oo adeegsada habab ka duwan xalalka kale ee ilaalinta qorraxda. Waxyaabaha kale ee laga walwalo waxaa ka mid ah, hay'addu waxay baareysaa in buufisyadu ay waxyeello u geysan karaan marka la neefsado. Sahanka ay sameysay Kooxda Environmental Working Group ayaa daaha ka qaaday in mid ka mid ah afarta muraayadood ee qorraxda ee laga iibiyo Mareykanka ay tahay badeeco lagu buufiyo. 'Dadku waxay jecel yihiin buufisyada sababtoo ah way dhaqso badan yihiin in la mariyo oo ay daboolaan meel ballaaran,' ayuu yiri Dr. Darrell Rigel, oo ah dhakhtar maqaarka ah oo ku sugan New York. 'Dhibaatadu waxay tahay inaad badanaa mariyso laba lakab.' article_content: By Mark Duell Published: 10:37 EST, 24 June 2013 | Updated: 11:23 EST, 24 June 2013 A woman gave a feeding bottle containing bleach to a stranger's baby, a court heard. The 11-month-old boy drank some of the liquid and vomited after being handed the bottle in a McDonald’s branch in Eltham, south-east London, Woolwich Crown Court heard. Elaine Joyner, 53, from Deptford, south-east London, is charged with administering a poison or noxious substance to endanger life, but Judge Andrew Lees ruled that she was unfit to plead. A trial proceeded in her absence to determine if Joyner committed the act. Peter Clark, prosecuting, told the jury that the incident occurred last September at the McDonald’s branch. He stated: ‘The prosecution says Elaine Joyner gave a complete stranger’s baby a feeding bottle containing a poisonous or noxious substance, a fluid containing bleach, or something very similar. The baby, 11-and-a-half months old, ingested some of the fluid and immediately became ill. He retched, vomited, and turned pale.’ His grandmother seized the bottle from the pram to prevent further harm, Clark added. The baby, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, recovered well with no long-term ill effects. ‘Ingestion of bleach can be fatal, particularly for a young child,’ Clark stated. Clark mentioned that CCTV from McDonald’s showed the pram but not the precise moment the bottle was handed over. ‘You see someone passing a bottle, and you can be sure it’s Elaine Joyner,’ he told the jury. Distinctive clothing and a carrier bag Joyner wore and carried that day were found at her home, counsel added. Other CCTV footage showed her walking in the street with a distinctive ‘waddle’ and entering McDonald’s. A statement from the child’s grandmother was read, stating that while looking after the baby in McDonald’s while his mother was at the counter, she saw him retching and dribbling. ‘I reached for a bottle in his pram and noticed it was orange with white milk particles and extremely frothy.’ ‘I realised he had drunk something we had not given him. Three black girls said a woman had walked past and given him a bottle.’ The mother stated: ‘Some random person gave my baby a bottle, which he drank from and vomited. I believed my baby had been poisoned.’ A statement was read from Joyner’s partner, Fred Warwick, 68, who had gone out that day. Joyner had told him she would be home for most of the day watching racing. She told him that evening that she had ‘popped out’ to Eltham but didn’t specify the time. The judge told the jury: ‘The defendant has been found unfit to stand trial. Based on evidence from two specialist medical practitioners, one instructed by the defense and one by the prosecution, she is mentally ill, unable to understand the proceedings, evidence, or give valid instructions to her legal team.’ He added that it was appropriate she did not attend. In these circumstances, there would be no finding of guilty or not guilty; the jury should decide whether she committed the alleged act. Trainee Detective Constable Sandra Voak identified Joyner from a CCTV photograph, recalling dealings with her in 2011. She stated she spent an hour with her that year, including 15 minutes in a car together. Asked if she was sure the person in the CCTV was the same woman, she stated: ‘I am absolutely certain it is the same person.’ The trial was adjourned until tomorrow. Comments are disabled for legal reasons.

Garyaqaanku waxa uu u sheegay xeerbeegtida: ‘Eedaysanaha waxaa lagu helay in aysan u qalmin in ay maxkamadda timaado. Tababare Booliis ah oo lagu magacaabo Sandra Voak ayaa aqoonsatay Joyner, iyadoo laga aqoonsaday sawir laga qaaday CCTV, waxaana ay xasuusatay wax kala qabasho ay la yeelatay sanadkii 2011. article_content: Serving in the U.S. military presents numerous challenges, including extended separations from loved ones. However, for David and Breanna Janssen, a unique opportunity has arisen: they are both deployed on the USS Harry S. Truman. For Breanna, this marks her initial deployment as a Gunner's Mate 3rd Class. David, her father, is the leading chief petty officer overseeing maintenance for the Seahawks, of Carrier Airborne Early Warning Squadron 126. Originally from Welsh, Louisiana, Breanna, age 21 and stationed in Norfolk, Virginia, expressed that having her father on board offers significant reassurance. 'It’s comforting knowing I always have someone to talk to, regardless of what’s happening.' David added that his extensive naval experience allows him to provide valuable guidance, especially since this deployment is likely his last. Breanna was inspired to join the Navy due to her father's distinguished career, which includes eight previous deployments. While the Navy often allows siblings to serve together, a parent and child serving simultaneously is less common. The USS Harry S. Truman, named after the 33rd U.S. President, was commissioned in 1993.

article_content: Unilever has initiated a limited recall of Skippy reduced-fat peanut butter spreads in 16 states due to the possible presence of salmonella. The voluntary recall, announced Friday, includes Skippy 'Reduced Fat Creamy' and 'Reduced Fat Super Chunk' varieties. Affected states are Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Iowa, Maine, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Dakota, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Wisconsin. Although no illnesses have been reported, the recall is a precautionary measure prompted by concerns that some products may be contaminated with salmonella. Unilever's press release indicated that routine sampling by inspectors revealed the potential contamination. The specific source and severity of the contamination were not disclosed in the release. Recalled products are packaged in 16.3-ounce plastic jars with UPC codes 048001006812 or 048001006782 and 'best-if-used-by' dates between May 16 and May 21, 2012. Consumers who have purchased the recalled product should discard it and contact Skippy at 1-800-453-3432 for a replacement coupon, according to Unilever. The Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey-based company is conducting the recall in cooperation with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which has posted Unilever's statement on its website. Salmonella infection typically lasts four to seven days; about 40,000 cases are reported annually in the U.S., according to the CDC. Symptoms include fever, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea, usually appearing 12 to 72 hours after infection. Most individuals recover without specific treatment; however, salmonella can be severe or fatal in young children, older adults, and those with weakened immune systems. The CDC advises individuals who suspect they may have contracted salmonella to consult a physician.

article_content: NAIROBI, Kenya (CNN) -- A Yemeni freighter has become the latest commercial vessel to be attacked in the pirate-infested Gulf of Aden, a Kenyan maritime official said Tuesday. A French frigate shadows a commercial ship leaving Djibouti harbor on its way to the Gulf of Aden. The last contact with the ship was made late last week, and the exact time of the hijacking remains unclear, according to Andrew Mwangura, the head of the Kenya Seafarers Association. No further details about the ship, its crew, or its cargo were immediately available, Mwangura said. His organization monitors the welfare of sailors captured by pirates. In recent months, dozens of ships have been attacked in the Gulf of Aden by pirates operating from largely lawless Somalia. This has prompted calls from commercial ship owners for a military blockade along the Somali coast to intercept pirate vessels heading out to sea. Peter Swift, managing director of the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners, stated that stronger naval action, including aerial support, is necessary to combat rampant piracy in the region. Watch more about the growing piracy problem » Currently, warships from several countries patrol an international maritime corridor, escorting some merchant ships and responding to distress calls in the area. However, the navies involved assert that it is virtually impossible to patrol the vast sea surrounding the gulf effectively. Meanwhile, a spokesman for the pirates holding a Saudi supertanker loaded with crude oil told the BBC that they have not yet set a ransom figure. He said the group has only spoken to intermediaries of the vessel's owners, describing them as untrustworthy. The pirate identified himself only as Daybad when he spoke late Monday to the BBC. Pirates seized the Sirius Star on November 15 in their most audacious hijacking to date. The vessel is carrying two million barrels of crude oil, valued at approximately $100 million. Elsewhere, the head of U.S. military operations in Africa has said that he does not have any evidence that Somali pirates are connected to al Qaeda. The Africom chief, Army Gen. William 'Kip' Ward, told The Associated Press on Tuesday that the chaos off Somalia's high seas reflects the country's political instability. Asked about alleged connections between pirates and al Qaeda, he said: 'I think that's a concern that we all would have.' However, he added that he doesn't have 'any evidence that pirates have links to al Qaeda.'

Bilihii u dambeeyay, tobanaan markab ayaa lagu weeraray Gacanka Cadmeed iyagoo ay weerareen burcad badeed ka soo jeeda Soomaaliya oo inta badan sharcigu ka jiro. Tani waxay dhalisay baaqyo ka yimid mulkiilayaasha maraakiibta ganacsiga oo ku baaqaya in xannibaad milatari lagu soo rogo xeebaha Soomaaliya si loo horjoogsado maraakiibta burcad badeeda ah ee badda u soo baxaya. Peter Swift, maamulaha guud ee Ururka Caalamiga ah ee Milkiilayaasha Taangiyada Madaxa Bannaan, ayaa sheegay in tallaabooyin ciidan oo xooggan, oo ay ku jiraan taageero dhanka cirka ah, ay lagama maarmaan u yihiin si loola dagaallamo burcad badeeda baahsan ee gobolka. Laakiin ciidamada badda ee ku lugta leh ayaa sheegaya inay ficil ahaan suurtogal ahayn in la ilaaliyo badda ballaaran ee ku hareeraysan gacanka. Dhanka kale, afhayeen u hadlay burcad badeeda haysata markab weyn oo Sucuudi ah oo saliid ceeriin ah ka buuxdo ayaa BBC u sheegay in aanay weli go'aamin wax madax furasho ah. Waxaa uu sheegay in kooxdu ay la hadashay oo keliya dhex dhexaadiyeyaasha milkiilayaasha markabka, isaga oo ku tilmaamay kuwo aan la isku hallayn karin. Burcad badeedda ayaa magaciisa ku sheegay Daybad oo keliya markii uu habeenimadii Isniinta la hadlay BBC. Burcad badeeddu waxay qabsadeen Sirius Star 15-kii Noofambar weerarkoodii ugu xumaa ilaa hadda. Taliyaha Africom, Gen. William 'Kip' Ward, ayaa u sheegay The Associated Press Talaadadii in fowdada ka jirta badda sare ee Soomaaliya ay ka tarjumayso fowdada siyaasadeed ee dalka. Isaga oo wax laga weydiiyay xiriirada la sheegay ee ka dhexeeya burcad badeeda iyo al-Qaacida, waxa uu yidhi: 'Waxaan u malaynayaa in taasi ay tahay welwel aan dhammaanteen qabno.' article_content: In a shocking turn of events, the family of Brandon Majewski, a 17-year-old who tragically died in 2012 after being struck by an SUV while cycling, is now facing a lawsuit from the driver involved. Sharlene Simon, the driver, is seeking $1.35 million, claiming emotional distress and alleging negligence on Brandon's part and from two other cyclists who were injured in the same incident near his home in Alcona. The lawsuit also names the county, citing poor road maintenance. Venetta Mlynczyk, Brandon's mother, expressed her devastation, questioning how Simon could seek to profit from her son's death and claiming to experience pain herself. Brian Cameron, the family's lawyer, conveyed his disbelief, stating he had never encountered a situation where someone sued the child they killed and that it was too upsetting to deliver the news by phone. Simon's legal representative, Michael Ellis, stated that while Ms. Simon empathizes with the cyclists' families for the losses they have sustained, she too has suffered and relives the incident daily, leading to post-traumatic stress disorder and an inability to return to work. Ellis argues the cyclists were riding carelessly on an unlit road at 1:30 am without proper reflectors, suggesting that nothing could have prevented the collision. In response, Brandon's father, Derek Majewski, refutes claims of negligence, asserting that children have the right to make mistakes and that the bikes were equipped with reflectors that would have been visible. Adding to the family's sorrow, Brandon's brother, Devon, passed away six months after the accident after taking pills and alcohol. Cameron has initiated a counter-suit against Simon to recoup medical and funeral costs, alleging she was speeding, possibly intoxicated, and possibly using her cellphone at the time of the accident. article_content: A new treatment uses a two-stage approach to stop cancers from growing and then destroy them from within. Medical experts in the UK have made a significant breakthrough in their research to manage breast cancer for a longer period. A new drug, T-DM1, has been tested and proven to slow the progression of the disease more effectively than current treatments, offering renewed hope for patients. The Freeman Hospital in Newcastle was one of several centers worldwide to test the new treatment for advanced breast cancer. Results from the study also indicate that T-DM1 significantly reduces the side effects associated with chemotherapy. While T-DM1 is undergoing further trials, this discovery is considered a major advancement. Dr. Mark Verrill, a consultant medical oncologist at the Newcastle Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, played a crucial role in the study, which focused on an advanced form of the disease known as HER2-positive. He stated: 'For the first time in breast cancer treatment, we have been able to significantly extend patients’ remission time while also minimizing the side effects of chemotherapy.' 'This is a promising development because HER2-positive breast cancer is highly aggressive. Once it reaches an advanced stage, it becomes challenging to treat, and there is a critical need for new, effective treatments like T-DM1 to improve the prognosis for women with this aggressive disease.' T-DM1 is classified as an 'antibody-drug conjugate', the first medicine of its kind for breast cancer. It combines the precision of the HER2-targeted antibody, Herceptin, with the potency of the chemotherapy agent, DM1, into a single therapy. T-DM1 is designed to selectively target and destroy cancerous cells through a two-stage mechanism. First, it binds to the cancer growth, inhibiting signals that promote tumor enlargement and spread. Then, it penetrates the cell’s defenses, releasing a concentrated dose of chemotherapy to eliminate it from within. The study’s results have been positively received by Joanne Smith, a breast cancer survivor from Whickham, Gateshead. The 41-year-old, diagnosed in 2005 and treated for over four years, said: 'Any advancements that help people overcome breast cancer are positive and greatly appreciated.' 'It’s wonderful that progress is being made, especially with the North East playing a role.' Study results demonstrate that more patients responded favorably to T-DM1 for an extended duration compared to the current standard treatment of lapatinib plus capecitabine chemotherapy. Researchers believe that attaching a potent chemotherapy agent to an antibody, such as Herceptin, could revolutionize the treatment of other types of breast cancer in the future. T-DM1 is currently being trialed in the earlier stages of the disease, where chemotherapy-induced side effects, such as diarrhea and hair loss, significantly impact patients. The drug is not yet approved for general use. However, based on the study’s findings, an application for its approval will be submitted in the UK and Europe. Following authorization from the European Medicines Agency, T-DM1 could potentially be available to patients in the UK within a year.

Natiijooyinka ka soo baxay daraasaddan waxaa si wanaagsan u soo dhaweysay Joanne Smith, oo ah qof ka badbaaday kansarka naasaha oo ka timid Whickham, Gateshead. Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay aaminsan yihiin in ku-xiridda daawada kiimoterabi ah oo awood leh antibody, sida Herceptin, ay beddeli karto daawaynta noocyada kale ee kansarka naasaha mustaqbalka. T-DM1 waxaa hadda lagu tijaabinayaa marxaladaha hore ee cudurka, halkaas oo waxyeellooyinka ay keento kiimoterabigu, sida shubanka iyo timo daadashada, ay si weyn u saameeyaan bukaannada. Daawadu weli looma oggola isticmaalka guud. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, iyada oo lagu saleynayo natiijooyinka daraasaddan, codsi oggolaansho ayaa laga gudbin doonaa UK iyo Yurub. article_content: One day, with my 3-year-old twins, I bravely faced subway stairs and train changes to reach the Museum of Natural History. I proudly took snapshots by the Apatosaurus and shared fun facts about the Jurassic period. I felt like an awesome mom! We then visited the gift shop for a treat. My son Theo chose the astronaut area. I showed him three options to make him feel in control. But he whined, 'No, astronaut!' and threw the toys down screaming after I pointed one out. After ten minutes and a freeze-dried ice cream disaster, I left, feeling like the worst mom, embarrassed and tired. It turns out that museum scene wasn't entirely my fault. Tantrums are normal, says Michael Potegal, Ph.D., a neuropsychologist. He found toddler outbursts are a normal biological response to frustration, similar to yawning when tired. Science can even predict tantrums! Kids between 18 months and 4 years are naturally inclined to misbehave, he explains. So, it's not always 'nurture' to blame. Let's check out the brain. The prefrontal cortex (PFC), behind the eyebrows, manages emotions and social behavior. It's still developing at age 4. That immaturity might boost language skills, says a University of Pennsylvania report. So, difficult behavior may be an evolutionary trade-off for communication. Kids have mushy brains and also experience stress. Psychologist Gina Mireault, Ph.D., notes that kids think magically and find ordinary events scary. Constant anxiety can make kids prone to tantrums. This anxiety releases cortisol, the 'fight or flight' hormone, which may lead to unclear thinking. Mild anxiety is normal, but constant stress turns kids into 'tantrum juice' primed to explode. When your child tantrums, ask, 'What's the purpose?' If it's for attention, ignore it, advises Potegal. My friend Mana Heydarpour learned this when her daughter yelled, 'I don't like you!' Potegal calls getting angry in response the 'Anger Trap.' Avoid the 'Sadness Trap' too. Comforting during a tantrum reinforces it. Instead, say, 'I'm sorry you're upset. We'll talk when you calm down.' Heydarpour says this helps. But ignoring 'escape' tantrums (when they avoid tasks) won't work. Instead, gently force compliance after a warning. If they resist, continue and then use time-out. This shows their protests didn't work and there are consequences. Toddlers are intense but tantrums are usually short, around three minutes, says Potegal. After a tantrum, they move on quickly due to their immature PFC. So, enjoy the post-tantrum cuddle! A tantrum's timeline: 0 sec: Meltdown starts. 30 sec: Foot stomping means it will be short. 90 sec: Screaming peaks. 3.5 min: It's over, they want comfort. 6 min: They're acting normal. 10 min: Long fits need a doctor's visit.

Cilmi-nafsiga yaqaan Gina Mireault, Ph.D., ayaa xusay in carruurtu si sixir ah u fikiraan oo ay u arkaan dhacdooyinka caadiga ah inay yihiin kuwo cabsi leh. Walaac joogto ah ayaa ka dhigi kara carruurta inay u nugul yihiin xanaaqa. Walaacani wuxuu sii daayaa cortisol, hormoonka 'dagaal ama carar', kaas oo horseedi kara fikir aan caddayn. Walaac fudud ayaa caadi ah, laakiin cadaadis joogto ah ayaa carruurta u roga 'cabitaan xanaaqa' oo diyaar u ah inay qarxaan. Marka ilmahaagu xanaaqo, is weydii, 'Waa maxay ujeeddadu?' Haddii ay tahay mid soo jiidasho leh, iska illow, ayuu kula taliyay Potegal. Saaxiibaday Mana Heydarpour ayaa tan baratay markii gabadheeda ay ku qaylisay, 'Kuma jecli!' Potegal wuxuu ugu yeeraa ka jawaab celinta caro 'Dabin Cadho'. Ka fogow 'Dabin Murugo' sidoo kale. Qaboojinta inta lagu jiro xanaaqa ayaa xoojinaysa dabeecadda xun. Taas bedelkeeda, dheh, 'Waan ka xumahay inaad xanaaqsan tahay. Waan hadli doonnaa markaad degto.' Heydarpour wuxuu sheegay in tani ay caawiso. Laakiin iska indho tirka xanaaqa 'baxsiga' (marka ay ka fogaadaan hawlaha) ma shaqayn doono. Taas bedelkeeda, si tartiib ah u qasab u hogaansanaanta ka dib digniin. Haddii ay iska caabiyaan, sii wad ka dibna isticmaal wakhti nasasho. Tani waxay muujinaysaa in mudaaharaadkoodu uusan shaqayn oo ay jiraan cawaaqib. Carruurta yaryari way daran yihiin laakiin xanaaqa badanaa waa gaaban yahay, qiyaastii saddex daqiiqo, ayuu yiri Potegal. Xanaaqa ka dib, si dhakhso ah ayay u socdaan sababtoo ah PFC-gooda oo aan qaan-gaarin. Marka, ku raaxayso isku duubnida xanaaqa ka dib! Jadwalka xanaaqa: 0 ilbiriqsi: Burburku wuu bilaabmaa. 30 ilbiriqsi: Lugaha oo la tumo waxay ka dhigan tahay inay gaaban doonto. 90 ilbiriqsi: Qayladu way kor u kacdaa. 3.5 daqiiqo: Way dhammaatay, waxay rabaan raaxo. 6 daqiiqo: Si caadi ah ayay u dhaqmayaan. 10 daqiiqo: Xanaaqa dheer wuxuu u baahan yahay booqasho dhakhtar.

article_content: In Cardiff, as horse-showing experts convened for the Horse of the Year competition, the stakes were high. However, few anticipated the triumph of three-year-old Fenton Kirkland. Barely past his first steps and not yet in school, the toddler and his Shetland pony, Toffee, navigated the three rounds effortlessly, securing the top prize and surpassing their 30 adult competitors. Fenton Kirkland, a three-year-old, triumphed over 30 adults, winning the gold cup and best of show rosette with his Shetland pony. Competitors are judged on style, an aspect they dedicate months to perfecting. The inseparable pair, of matching heights, were recognized for their appearance, behavior, and style at the annual Sunnybank Equestrian Centre contest in Rudry, near Cardiff. Facing men and women in formal bowler hats, Fenton sported a tilted flat cap and paraded Toffee around the ring. Judges praised Fenton's innate handling skills, far exceeding his age. Toffee earned top marks for his appearance and personality. Fenton received Toffee as a third birthday gift last March and has since practiced daily with the pony. His mother, Donna, 30, remarked: 'Fenton and Toffee are a remarkable duo.' 'They competed against everyone and emerged victorious with the gold cup and rosette. It was only Fenton's second competition with Toffee, and we were overjoyed by his win.' 'Strangers in the arena were so impressed that they requested photos with him.' The young boy, from Nantyglo, near Ebbw Vale, South Wales, is following in the footsteps of his aunt, Sharon Howells, a horse-showing enthusiast for over 10 years. Mrs. Howells commented: 'The atmosphere was electric, filled with cheers and applause.' 'He ran down the arena with confidence, and despite his small size, he performed admirably.' 'Fenton adores animals—horses, tractors, farms—and even cares for two chickens.' 'Given his early success, he'll likely compete at the Horse of the Year show soon, and I'm confident he'll excel.' A horse show spokesman stated: 'Despite being only three, Fenton is skilled in handling his pony. They make an excellent team.' 'Fenton and Toffee were assessed on their presentation and teamwork in the show ring.' 'Judges seek strong harmony between the pony and handler—Fenton and Toffee were the best.' 'Fenton's charming attire undoubtedly contributed to his success; he truly looked the part.'
